title: Model Invocation Stability and Tooling Contract
author: Aisha Kapoor
content:
Summary:

This document defines a cross-team contract for model invocation stability and the runtime tooling surface used for interactive function/tool calls, structured responses, and side-effectful tool integrations. The goal is to provide clear guarantees that let client libraries, SDKs, and higher-level orchestration safely rely on model behavior and tool integrations across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Scope and motivation:

- Applies to all model-serving endpoints that support: function/tool-calling, structured-output schemas, and delayed side-effect execution hooks (examples: call_tool, stash_to_db, emit_event).
- Motivated by a set of production incidents where partial tool invocations or non-deterministic schema shapes caused duplicate downstream effects and customer-visible inconsistency.
- This contract harmonizes: API semantics, invocation lifecycle (prepare/execute/confirm/cancel), observability expectations, testing gates, and rollout controls.

Key guarantees (consumer-facing):

1) At-least-once vs exactly-once semantics
   - Default serving semantics remain at-least-once for model-generated tool-call intents.
   - Exactly-once guarantees are available when the tool integration implements an idempotency token and an acknowledgement API (see "Idempotency handshake" below).

2) Invocation lifecycle events
   - A stable sequence of events MUST be emitted for every model-invocation that contains a tool-call: PREPARE -> TRY_EXECUTE -> EXECUTE_ACK -> COMPLETE or CANCEL.
   - Event types are emitted to telemetry and tracing with these keys: invocation.id, invocation.attempt (int), invocation.status, tool.name, tool.version, model.variant.

3) Tool manifest discovery and compatibility
   - Tool integrations MUST publish a stable manifest (tool-manifest.json) including: name, semantic_version, idempotency_capabilities (none|client-provided-token|handshake), validation_schema (json-schema v2019-09), and allowed_side_effects (list).
   - Runtimes MUST validate incoming model tool-call payloads against the declared validation_schema before attempting execution and emit validation.errors with severity levels.

Operational SLOs and thresholds:

- Successful execution SLI: 99.9% of TRY_EXECUTE->COMPLETE within 1s for local (in-host) sync tool calls; 99.0% within 5s for cross-service calls (measured over 1d rolling window).
- Transient failure budget: callers are allowed up to 0.1% of invocations that reach EXECUTE_ACK but ultimately CANCEL due to precondition failures.
- Telemetry availability: all invocation lifecycle events MUST be emitted; loss of >0.5% of invocation.events per hour triggers an alert.

Observability and telemetry contract:

- Minimum telemetry fields (exported with every invocation event): 
  - invocation.id (UUID), invocation.attempt (int), invocation.status (PREPARE|TRY_EXECUTE|EXECUTE_ACK|COMPLETE|CANCEL), model.name, model.version, tool.name, tool.version, latency_ms, trace_id, tenant.id
- Structured logs: tool execution paths MUST include a structured log line containing invocation.id and attempt for any non-OK outcome.
- Tracing: spans MUST be correlated using trace_id and include a span attribute "invocation.phase" with the lifecycle phase.

Idempotency handshake (recommended pattern for exactly-once):

1) Client (model runtime) includes idempotency_token in TRY_EXECUTE when tool.manifest.idempotency_capabilities != "none".
2) Tool service exposes /tools/{name}/ack to verify token and reserve the execution slot. The ack returns: {ack_id, reserved_until_iso, precheck_status}.
3) Model runtime calls /tools/{name}/execute with ack_id. If network failure occurs after ack but before confirmation, the runtime may retry execute with the same ack_id for exactly-once semantics.

Validation and testing gates before rollout:

- Contract compliance tests (automated):
  1) Schema validation tests: randomly generated payloads that must be rejected/accepted according to tool schema.
  2) Lifecycle event fuzz tests: simulate partial failures and verify emitted event sequence and deduplication behavior.
  3) Idempotency stress tests: exercise concurrent retries and verify no duplicate side effects for tools claiming handshake capability.
- Manual checklist before canary:
  - Confirm tool.manifest published in runtime registry and accessible by all regions.
  - Run a 24h canary at 1% traffic using synthetic prompts that exercise function-calling boundaries (max args, boundary types).
  - Validate SLI/alerting rule firing accuracy against synthetic trace generation.

Rollout and rollback knobs:

- Feature flagging: runtimes must gate any change in invocation semantics behind a runtime feature flag "tooling.experimental.invocation_semantics" with safe default off for private deployments.
- Canary policy: increment traffic percentage doubling every 6 hours if no critical alerts; abort on any SLO regression > 0.5% or any duplicate side-effect detection.
- Automatic rollback: if duplicate side-effect detector finds a duplicate within 24h, the runtime must automatically disable the variant and notify owners.

Failure modes and remediation playbook:

1) Validation failures (invalid payloads)
   - Action: reject with 400, emit validation.errors, route sample to /tooling/validation-database for analysis.
   - Owner: runtime-tooling team.
2) Ack timeouts (idempotency ack expired)
   - Action: mark attempt CANCEL, surface metric tool.ack.timeouts, and trigger backpressure policy to caller.
   - Owner: tool-owner on-call.
3) Duplicate side-effects detected
   - Action: initiate incident, freeze canary rollout, issue customer-facing mitigation if external side effects observed.
   - Owner: incident commander (rotating SRE).

Security and privacy constraints:

- Tool manifests MUST declare data retention expectations and any external network egress.
- Sensitive tools (declared in allowed_side_effects) MUST require tenant consent and be documented in customer-facing policies for Private deployments.

Implementation notes (runtime and SDK):

- Runtime MUST include a compact instrument with bounded memory per invocation (max 5 KB metadata persisted across retries).
- SDKs SHOULD expose helpers for: generating idempotency tokens, validating schema locally, and wiring lifecycle event consumers to application logs.

Example tool-manifest.json (required fields):

{
  "name": "email-sender",
  "semantic_version": "1.2.0",
  "idempotency_capabilities": "handshake",
  "validation_schema": { "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", "type": "object", "required": ["to", "body"] },
  "allowed_side_effects": ["send-email"],
  "contact_owner": "tools-team@redwood.ai"
}

Ownership and escalation:

- Runtime-tooling team (primary) — owner of lifecycle event emission, validation gating, and SDK helpers.
- Model-onboarding team (secondary) — approves changes to model variant compatibility with tools.
- Tool-owner (per integration) — responsible for manifest accuracy, ack endpoint, and side-effect safeguards.
- Escalation path: tool-owner -> runtime-tooling -> SRE -> Security if data exfiltration suspected.

Open decisions (ADR seeds):

- Whether to make exactly-once the default for all internal tool calls in Dedicated deployments (tradeoffs: complexity vs stronger safety guarantees).
- Standardizing a single JSON Schema draft across all tool manifests (compatibility across SDKs).

Appendices:

A. Example event log (newline-delimited JSON):
{ "invocation.id": "7f9a3d2b-2c4e-4c6a-b1f2-8a0f3e6b1c2a", "invocation.attempt": 1, "invocation.status": "PREPARE", "model.name": "llama-variant-x", "tool.name": "email-sender", "timestamp": "2026-02-10T14:23:05Z" }
{ "invocation.id": "7f9a3d2b-2c4e-4c6a-b1f2-8a0f3e6b1c2a", "invocation.attempt": 1, "invocation.status": "TRY_EXECUTE", "latency_ms": 12 }
{ "invocation.id": "7f9a3d2b-2c4e-4c6a-b1f2-8a0f3e6b1c2a", "invocation.status": "EXECUTE_ACK", "ack_id": "ack-41ac", "reserved_until": "2026-02-10T14:23:35Z" }
{ "invocation.id": "7f9a3d2b-2c4e-4c6a-b1f2-8a0f3e6b1c2a", "invocation.status": "COMPLETE" }

B. Quick checklist for tool owners before onboarding:
- Publish tool-manifest.json in runtime registry.
- Provide integration tests that exercise idempotency and schema boundaries.
- Confirm /ack and /execute endpoints meet latency expectations (p95 < 200ms local).

C. Related artifacts:
- SDK helper spec (link to eng-developer-experience docs).
- Duplicate side-effect detector runbook (link to eng-sre/runbooks).

Contributors: runtime-tooling, model-onboarding, eng-sre, platform-security.

Next steps:
